subject: Post-call: hosting & audit evidence required for Medbridge POC
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Keller <tom.keller@medbridge.health>, Alice Park <alice.park@medbridge.health>
Cc: 
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: hosting & audit evidence required for Medbridge POC

Tom / Alice — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our end.

Call recap (short):
- Goal: 6-week POC for inpatient medication reconciliation workflows (PHI in scope).
- Key security asks you raised: BAA, SOC2 Type II evidence, network isolation for VPC, and audit access for logs.
- Timeline: procurement and security review want artifacts this week to kick off legal + infra onboarding.

Options we discussed (one-line):
- Hosted API: fastest to ship (no infra work). Good if you can accept tokens routed through Redwood-hosted regions; we provide BAA + SOC2 artifacts.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool in our environment; provides stronger tenancy isolation and predictable capacity (supports stricter SLAs).
- Private VPC / On-prem: customer-managed VNet or on-prem appliance (longest lead time; required for certain regulatory controls).

For procurement/security: can you confirm (a) whether MedBridge can accept our hosted API under a signed BAA, or (b) if you need a Private VPC or Dedicated instance? If you lean private/Dedicated, let us know which cloud/region (Azure US-East, AWS us-east-1, on-prem) and any specific network requirements.

Attachments: sending our SOC2 summary and a draft BAA for your legal team to review (see attached).

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm preferred hosting option (Hosted / Dedicated / Private VPC) and any hard constraints (e.g., no shared tenancy).
2) If Private VPC or Dedicated is needed, we schedule a short technical call (30m) with our Solutions Engineer + your network/security team to validate connectivity and firewall rules.
3) We share the SOC2 Type II PDF and BAA draft now. If helpful, Grace can produce a one-page network diagram and a list of audit logs we can provide.

If you can reply with hosting preference and the primary procurement/security contact, we’ll move artifacts straight to them.

Best,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers from our side: we are processing PHI for the POC, so a signed BAA is non-negotiable. Our security team has said they require vendor SOC2 Type II evidence.

On hosting preference: procurement has a preference for a Private VPC (we run strict network controls) but they also asked for a pricing comparison vs Dedicated capacity — if Dedicated is materially cheaper and provides required isolation, that could work. On-prem is only considered if there are blockers for VPC.

Specific asks:
- Can Redwood provision into our Azure subscription / VNet (we can share peering details) or do you only support VPC peering from your Azure tenant?
- Do you have a short network diagram we can share with our network ops?
- Ballpark pricing for Dedicated vs Private VPC for a 4-week POC (expected ~60k token/day).

Looping Alice (procurement) — Alice, can you confirm the contract timeline? We’d like to get BAA + SOC2 artifacts to legal today if possible.

Thanks — Tom
Director, Product — MedBridge Health
Tom.Keller@medbridge.health

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: hosting & audit evidence required for Medbridge POC

Tom / Alice — great, thanks. Answers inline and next steps below.

Short answers:
- Azure VNet integration: yes — we support peering into customer Azure subscriptions (Private VPC model). We also offer Dedicated capacity in our tenancy with stricter tenancy isolation if you cannot operate peering.
- Network diagram: attaching a 1-page sketch that highlights peering, allowed ports, and audit log flows.
- Pricing: putting a quick ballpark in the thread below — Grace, Rishi, please confirm numbers and any minimums.

Quick hosting comparison (for procurement):
- Hosted API: pros: fastest (hours); cons: shared control plane and cross-tenant routing — still BAA-compatible for many customers, but not suitable where the customer requires inbound peering or full VNet control.
- Dedicated capacity: pros: single-tenant GPU pool, stronger SLO and throughput guarantees, faster to stand up than full VPC peering; cons: higher committed cost and provisioning lead time (typically 1–2 weeks).
- Private VPC (Azure peering) / On-prem: pros: maximum network isolation, audit log forwarding, customer-managed network controls; cons: longest lead time (2–4+ weeks), needs coordination with your infra team.

Next steps I propose:
1) Alice — please confirm if procurement will accept hosted API + BAA or requires Private VPC/Dedicated.
2) If you need Private VPC, can you share the preferred Azure region and a point of contact for network ops?
3) Grace / Rishi — please attach SOC2 Type II PDF, the BAA draft, and the 1-page network sketch. Also confirm initial pricing ballpark for Dedicated vs Private VPC for the POC.

Ben

Ben / Rishi — attaching the artifacts for MedBridge. See brief notes below.

Attachments included:
- SOC2-Type2-report-2026.pdf (redacted summary; full report available under NDA)
- BAA-template-redwood.docx (our standard template; legal can redline)
- network-architecture-sketch.png (1-page; shows Azure VNet peering and required ports)

Notes / guidance:
- SOC2: we can provide the summary publicly but will need an NDA for the full evidence package (testimonials, control matrices). Recommend we surface the redacted PDF to the MedBridge security team now and offer a secure share for the full pack if required.
- Azure peering: MedBridge will need to open 443 (control plane) plus a few egress ports (listed in sketch). We can support private peering into their subscription; engineering will need the peering CIDR and an Azure point-of-contact.
- Pricing (ballpark for POC): Dedicated (single-tenant reserved pool): ~$18k/week; Private VPC (peered into customer Azure, managed by us): ~$24k/week (includes VPC setup and extra audit retention). These are initial estimates — Rishi, please update if you want different numbers or minimums to apply.

Recommended immediate next actions:
1) Ben to push the redacted SOC2 + BAA draft to Alice/legal.
2) Tom/Alice to confirm hosting preference and provide Azure region + networking contact if they want Private VPC.
3) Schedule 30m technical call next week (Grace + Rishi + MedBridge network ops) to validate firewall rules and timelines.

Grace O'Connor
